category: Stateflow: chart objects, action language, temporal logic & API (extended)
description: Stateflow chart building blocks beyond the core Chart/State/Transition entries: graphical objects (states, transitions, junctions, functions, boxes, atomic subcharts), state and transition action syntax, temporal-logic and change-detection operators, events and messages, active state data, chart properties, and the Stateflow API classes and utility functions used to build charts from MATLAB.

tools.name: State
tools.description: A Stateflow state describes an operating mode of the chart. States can contain substates with exclusive (OR) decomposition, where exactly one substate is active, or parallel (AND) decomposition, where all substates are active together. The state label holds the name followed by entry, during, exit and on-event actions.
tools.usage:
Stateflow Editor: drag the State tool onto the canvas; label syntax:
Name
entry: ...
during: ...
exit: ...
on evt: ...

parameters.name: Decomposition
parameters.description: 'EXCLUSIVE_OR' (default) or 'PARALLEL_AND' for the substates of a state or chart.

parameters.name: ExecutionOrder
parameters.description: For parallel states, the order in which sibling states execute.

parameters.name: HasOutputData
parameters.description: Create active state output data for the state.

tools.notes: Parallel states are drawn with dashed borders and numbered execution order. Use the in operator to test whether another state is active.

tools.name: entry / during / exit (state actions)
tools.description: Keywords in a state label that define when actions execute: entry (en) when the state becomes active, during (du) on every chart execution while it remains active and no transition is taken, exit (ex) when it is left. 'on event_name:' and 'on after(...)' actions run only when the event or temporal condition occurs.

parameters.name: entry / en
parameters.description: Executed once on state entry.

parameters.name: during / du
parameters.description: Executed each time step the state stays active.

parameters.name: exit / ex
parameters.description: Executed once on state exit.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: Executed on an event, message or temporal condition.

tools.notes: In Moore charts only entry/during-style output assignment in states is allowed; Mealy charts compute outputs on transitions.

tools.name: Transition
tools.description: A directed line between states or junctions that moves chart activity when its label is satisfied. The label has the form trigger[condition]{condition_action}/{transition_action}; all parts are optional and an unlabeled transition is always valid.

parameters.name: event / message
parameters.description: Trigger that must be present (optional).

parameters.name: [condition]
parameters.description: Boolean guard evaluated when the transition is tested.

parameters.name: {condition_action}
parameters.description: Executed as soon as the condition is true, before the destination is known to be valid.

parameters.name: /transition_action
parameters.description: Executed only when the complete path to a destination state is valid.

parameters.name: ExecutionOrder
parameters.description: Order in which outgoing transitions from the same source are tested.

tools.notes: Outgoing transitions are tested in execution order (shown as numbers on the lines); enable 'User specified state/transition execution order' to control it explicitly.

tools.name: Default Transition
tools.description: A transition with no source that marks which state (or junction path) becomes active when its parent chart or superstate with exclusive decomposition is entered. Every exclusive-OR level must have exactly one default transition path.
tools.usage: Stateflow Editor: Default Transition tool; programmatically a Stateflow.Transition with only a Destination

parameters.name: Destination
parameters.description: State or junction entered by default.

parameters.name: SourceEndpoint
parameters.description: Canvas coordinates of the free (source) end of the arrow.

tools.notes: A missing default transition produces a 'state inconsistency' error during simulation. Default transitions may carry conditions and actions, e.g. to choose the initial state from an input.

tools.name: Connective Junction
tools.description: A decision point that splits or joins transition segments so that one transition path can branch on several conditions. Combined with transitions it models if-then-else logic, for-loops and flow charts without states.
tools.usage: Stateflow Editor: Connective Junction tool; API: j = Stateflow.Junction(parent); j.Type = 'CONNECTIVE'

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: 'CONNECTIVE'.

parameters.name: Position.Center / Position.Radius
parameters.description: Location and size on the canvas.

tools.notes: Always provide an unconditional fallback branch from a junction to avoid dead-ends. The Pattern Wizard (Chart > Add Pattern in Chart) generates standard if/loop junction patterns.

tools.name: History Junction
tools.description: Placed inside a superstate, a history junction makes the superstate re-enter the substate that was most recently active instead of following the default transition. Use it to resume a mode after an interruption.
tools.usage: Stateflow Editor: History Junction tool (H); API: j = Stateflow.Junction(state); j.Type = 'HISTORY'

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: 'HISTORY'.

tools.notes: History applies only to the level it is placed in, not recursively to deeper substates.

tools.name: Graphical Function
tools.description: A function defined by a flow chart of transitions and connective junctions, callable from state and transition actions. Use it for reusable decision logic or iterative algorithms expressed graphically.
tools.usage: Stateflow Editor: Graphical Function tool; signature label: [y1, y2] = fname(u1, u2)

parameters.name: LabelString
parameters.description: Function signature.

parameters.name: Function Inline Option
parameters.description: 'Auto', 'Inline' or 'Function' for code generation.

tools.notes: Scope follows placement: a function inside a state is visible only there. Programmatic class: Stateflow.Function.

tools.name: Box
tools.description: A grouping object that organises states and functions inside a chart and creates a separate namespace, without changing execution semantics (except that boxes affect execution order of parallel states). Used to keep large charts readable.
tools.usage: Stateflow Editor: Box tool; API: b = Stateflow.Box(parent)

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Box name, used to qualify contained objects (Box.fcn()).

tools.notes: Functions inside a box are called with dot notation, e.g. Utilities.clampVal(x, 0, 1).

tools.name: Atomic Subchart
tools.description: A self-contained subchart that behaves like a chart in its own right: it has its own data mapping, can be linked from a library for reuse across charts, can be simulated and code-generated independently, and only its own content recompiles after changes.
tools.usage: Right-click a state > Group & Subchart > Atomic Subchart; API: Stateflow.AtomicSubchart

parameters.name: Subchart
parameters.description: The contained chart content.

parameters.name: Data mapping
parameters.description: Maps atomic subchart data to data of the parent chart.

tools.notes: Atomic subcharts cannot access data of the parent by name directly; use explicit mapping. Useful for team development and unit testing of chart pieces.

tools.name: after
tools.description: Temporal-logic operator that becomes true after the associated state has been active for at least n occurrences of an event, n chart wake-ups (tick), or n units of simulation time. Used on transitions and in 'on' actions to model delays and timeouts.
tools.usage:
after(n, E)
after(n, tick)
after(n, sec) | after(n, msec) | after(n, usec)

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Count or time, may be an expression.

parameters.name: E / tick / sec / msec / usec
parameters.description: Base event, chart wake-ups, or absolute time unit.

tools.example:
% transition from Open to Closed after a 2.5 s timeout
after(2.5, sec)[~doorBlocked]
tools.notes: The counter resets each time the associated state is re-entered. Absolute-time operators in Simulink charts count simulation time and may need a fixed sample time for exact timing.

tools.name: before
tools.description: Temporal-logic operator that is true while the associated state has been active for fewer than n events, ticks or time units. Typically combined with a condition to accept an input only within a time window.
tools.usage:
before(n, E)
before(n, tick)
before(n, sec) | before(n, msec) | before(n, usec)

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Count or time limit.

parameters.name: E / tick / time unit
parameters.description: Base of the count.

tools.example:
% double-click detection: second click within 0.3 s
click[before(0.3, sec)]
tools.notes: before(n,E) and after(n,E) are complementary for the same state activation.

tools.name: at
tools.description: Temporal-logic operator that is true only at exactly the n-th occurrence of an event (or n-th chart wake-up) since the associated state became active. Useful for one-shot actions at a precise count.
tools.usage:
at(n, E)
at(n, tick)
at(n, sec)   % standalone MATLAB charts only

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Exact occurrence count.

parameters.name: E / tick
parameters.description: Base event or chart wake-ups.

tools.example:
Warmup
on at(100, tick): ready = true;
tools.notes: at(n, sec) is supported only in standalone charts in MATLAB; in Simulink charts use after for time. The tick form cannot be used when the chart has input events.

tools.name: every
tools.description: Temporal-logic operator that is true at every n-th occurrence of an event or every n-th chart wake-up while the associated state is active. Used for periodic actions inside a state.
tools.usage:
every(n, E)
every(n, tick)
every(n, sec)   % standalone MATLAB charts only

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Period in events or ticks.

parameters.name: E / tick
parameters.description: Base event or chart wake-ups.

tools.example:
Logging
on every(50, tick): sampleCount = sampleCount + 1;
tools.notes: Absolute-time every(n, sec) is not supported in charts in Simulink models; use a Function-Call Generator or rate-based logic instead.

tools.name: temporalCount
tools.description: Returns how many events, chart wake-ups or time units have passed since the associated state became active. Use it to compute elapsed counts for outputs or logic rather than only testing thresholds.

parameters.name: E / tick / time unit
parameters.description: What to count.

tools.example:
Charging
du: chargeTime = temporalCount(sec);
tools.notes: Resets when the state is re-entered.

tools.name: elapsed
tools.description: Returns the simulation time in seconds since the associated state became active; et is shorthand. Equivalent to temporalCount(sec).
tools.example:
Active
en, du: y = elapsed(sec);
tools.notes: The counter resets each time the state reactivates.

tools.name: duration
tools.description: Returns how long a condition has continuously been true since it became true (and the associated state became active). Ideal for debouncing and 'held for T seconds' requirements.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: Boolean expression on inputs (not on local or output data).

parameters.name: time unit
parameters.description: sec (default), msec or usec.

tools.example:
% leave state when pressure stayed above limit for more than 0.1 s
[duration(p > pMax) > 0.1]
tools.notes: Not supported in standalone MATLAB charts. Resets when the condition becomes false or the state exits.

tools.name: hasChanged
tools.description: Change-detection operator that returns true when a data value at the start of the current time step differs from its value at the start of the previous step. hasChangedFrom(data, v) and hasChangedTo(data, v) detect changes away from or to a specific value.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Chart input, local or output data (or an element/field of it).

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Value to compare against for hasChangedFrom/hasChangedTo.

tools.example: [hasChangedTo(gear, 1)]{shiftCount = shiftCount + 1;}
tools.notes: Also available in Test Sequence blocks. Requires discrete sample time semantics for predictable behaviour.

tools.name: in
tools.description: Returns true when the named state is active in the current time step. Used in conditions to coordinate parallel states without events.
tools.usage: in(state_name)   % state_name may be qualified, e.g. in(Engine.Running)

parameters.name: state_name
parameters.description: State name; qualify with parent names when ambiguous.

tools.example:
% in a parallel Display state:
[in(Engine.Fault)]{warningLamp = true;}
tools.notes: Active state output data is an alternative that exposes activity to Simulink.

tools.name: Active state output
tools.description: Chart or state option that creates output (or local) data reporting state activity: a Boolean for self activity, or an enumerated value naming the active child or leaf state. It removes the need for manual mode flags and makes modes visible to Simulink.
tools.usage: State/Chart properties > Create output for monitoring; API: obj.HasOutputData = true; obj.OutputMonitoringMode = ...

parameters.name: HasOutputData
parameters.description: true creates the active state data object.

parameters.name: OutputMonitoringMode
parameters.description: 'SelfActivity' (states, atomic subcharts), 'ChildActivity' or 'LeafStateActivity' (states and charts).

parameters.name: OutputData
parameters.description: The created Stateflow.Data object (name, scope, enumeration type name).

tools.notes: The generated enumeration type is named after the chart by default; rename it to share it with other models.

tools.name: ActionLanguage (chart property)
tools.description: Chooses the syntax of state and transition actions in a chart: MATLAB (default for new charts) or C. MATLAB action language supports MATLAB syntax, indexing from 1 and type inference; C action language uses C operators, zero-based indexing and explicit types.

parameters.name: 'MATLAB'
parameters.description: MATLAB syntax: x(1), ~=, ~, if-blocks in actions, one-based indexing.

parameters.name: 'C'
parameters.description: C syntax: x[0], !=, !, ++, pointer and address operators with custom code.

tools.example:
ch = sfroot().find('-isa', 'Stateflow.Chart', 'Path', 'myModel/Chart');
ch.ActionLanguage = 'C';
tools.notes: Changing language on an existing chart can make actions invalid; update the labels after switching.

tools.name: StateMachineType (chart property)
tools.description: Selects the chart semantics: Classic (full Stateflow semantics), Mealy (outputs depend on inputs and state, computed on transitions) or Moore (outputs depend only on state, computed in state actions). Mealy and Moore restrict syntax to guarantee the formal model.
tools.example: ch.StateMachineType = 'Moore';
tools.notes: Mealy/Moore charts must be discrete-time and cannot use input events of some kinds; the Model Advisor reports violations.

tools.name: ChartUpdate (chart property)
tools.description: Determines when a chart wakes up: inherited from its inputs, at a discrete sample time, or continuously (for charts with continuous-time state variables and zero-crossing detection).

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Applies only when ChartUpdate is 'DISCRETE'.

tools.example:
ch.ChartUpdate = 'DISCRETE';
ch.SampleTime = '0.001';
tools.notes: Charts with input events wake up on those events regardless of this setting.

tools.name: ExecuteAtInitialization (chart property)
tools.description: When true, the chart takes its default transitions and executes entry actions at time zero during model initialization, instead of at the first wake-up. This makes initial outputs consistent from the first step.
tools.example: ch.ExecuteAtInitialization = true;
tools.notes: Dialog label: 'Execute (enter) Chart At Initialization'. Not allowed for charts driven by function-call input events in some configurations.

tools.name: EnableNonTerminalStates (chart property)
tools.description: Enables super step semantics: in one time step the chart keeps taking valid transitions until it reaches a stable state configuration (or a maximum number of iterations), instead of taking at most one transition per step.

parameters.name: NonTerminalMaxCounts
parameters.description: Maximum number of transitions per super step.

parameters.name: NonTerminalUnstableBehavior
parameters.description: What to do if the maximum is reached without a stable state.

tools.example:
ch.EnableNonTerminalStates = true;
ch.NonTerminalMaxCounts = 100;
tools.notes: Dialog label: 'Enable Super Step Semantics'. Useful for event-free logic that must settle within one step.

tools.name: Stateflow.Data
tools.description: API object for data in a chart, state, box or function: inputs, outputs, locals, constants, parameters, data store memory and temporaries. Properties mirror the Property Inspector and Symbols pane.

parameters.name: Scope
parameters.description: 'Input', 'Output', 'Local', 'Constant', 'Parameter', 'Data Store Memory', 'Temporary'.

parameters.name: DataType
parameters.description: e.g. 'double', 'boolean', 'uint8', 'Enum: Mode', 'Bus: B', 'Inherit: Same as Simulink'.

parameters.name: Props.InitialValue / Props.Array.Size / Props.Range
parameters.description: Initial value, size and min/max.

tools.notes: Input and output data create chart ports in the order of their Port property.

tools.name: Stateflow.Event
tools.description: API object for an event: an input event (edge-triggered or function call) that wakes the chart, a local event broadcast inside the chart with send, or an output event that triggers downstream Simulink subsystems.

parameters.name: Scope
parameters.description: 'Input', 'Output' or 'Local'.

parameters.name: Trigger
parameters.description: For input/output events: 'Rising', 'Falling', 'Either' or 'Function call'.

tools.notes: Local event broadcasts can cause recursive chart execution; prefer messages or conditions in new designs.

tools.name: Stateflow.Message
tools.description: API object for a Stateflow message: a queued event carrying data. Input messages come from Simulink message lines (Send block, other charts); charts send output or local messages with send(M) and inspect them with receive, forward, discard, isvalid and length.

parameters.name: Scope
parameters.description: 'Input', 'Output' or 'Local'.

parameters.name: DataType
parameters.description: Type of the message payload M.data.

parameters.name: Queue settings
parameters.description: Queue capacity and type (FIFO, LIFO, priority) for input/local messages.

tools.notes: Unconsumed messages are discarded at the end of the time step unless forwarded; see the Sequence Viewer to debug message flow.

tools.name: Stateflow.Junction
tools.description: API class for connective and history junctions in a chart, state, box or function. Set Type to choose the junction kind and Position to place it.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: 'CONNECTIVE' or 'HISTORY'.

parameters.name: Position
parameters.description: Structure with Center and Radius.

tools.notes: Use sourcedTransitions / sinkedTransitions methods to navigate connected transitions.

tools.name: Stateflow.Function
tools.description: API class for graphical functions: flow-chart functions containing junctions and transitions that can be called in state and transition actions.

parameters.name: LabelString
parameters.description: Function signature.

parameters.name: InlineOption
parameters.description: 'Auto', 'Inline' or 'Function'.

tools.notes: Data objects created with Stateflow.Data(f) become the function's arguments or locals.

tools.name: Stateflow.Box
tools.description: API class for boxes that group states and functions in a chart to organise it and create a namespace.

parameters.name: Name / Position
parameters.description: Box name and canvas rectangle.

tools.notes: Objects are moved into a box by creating them with the box as parent.

tools.name: Stateflow.AtomicSubchart
tools.description: API class for atomic subcharts: independent chart components that can be reused from libraries, simulated and generated separately, and edited by different team members.

parameters.name: Name / Position
parameters.description: Subchart name and location.

parameters.name: Subchart
parameters.description: Handle to the contained chart object for editing its contents.

tools.notes: Supports OutputMonitoringMode 'SelfActivity' only for active state output.

tools.name: Stateflow.TruthTable
tools.description: API class for truth table functions inside charts: combinational decision logic described by a condition table and an action table, callable from actions.
tools.usage: tt = Stateflow.TruthTable(parent); tt.LabelString = 'y = decide(a, b)'; tt.ConditionTable = {...}; tt.ActionTable = {...};

parameters.name: ConditionTable
parameters.description: Cell array of condition descriptions, expressions and T/F/- decision columns.

parameters.name: ActionTable
parameters.description: Cell array of action descriptions and actions.

parameters.name: Language
parameters.description: 'MATLAB' or 'C' action syntax in the table.

tools.notes: The Truth Table block (Stateflow library) is the standalone Simulink block form of the same concept.

tools.name: Stateflow.EMFunction
tools.description: API class for MATLAB functions inside a chart: functions written in MATLAB code and called from state or transition actions, useful for numerical algorithms that are awkward to draw.

parameters.name: LabelString
parameters.description: Function signature.

parameters.name: Script
parameters.description: MATLAB code of the function body.

tools.notes: Code must be code-generation compatible (same subset as the MATLAB Function block).

tools.name: Stateflow.SLFunction
tools.description: API class for Simulink functions inside a chart: a function whose body is a Simulink subsystem, callable from state and transition actions. It lets charts call signal-processing or plant-model logic built from Simulink blocks.

parameters.name: LabelString
parameters.description: Function signature; the contained subsystem gets matching Inport/Outport blocks.

tools.notes: Blocks inside must use inherited sample times; the function executes like a function-call subsystem.

tools.name: sfsave
tools.description: Saves a model containing Stateflow charts to the current folder, optionally under a new name. It is the Stateflow counterpart of save_system for API scripts.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Open model to save.

parameters.name: newName
parameters.description: Optional new model name.

tools.notes: The model must be open and the current folder writable; save_system works equally well.

tools.name: sfclose
tools.description: Closes Stateflow chart editor windows: the most recently active chart, a named chart, or all charts.

parameters.name: chartName
parameters.description: Name of the chart to close, or 'all'.

tools.example: sfclose('all');
tools.notes: Closes editor windows only; use close_system to close the model.

tools.name: sflib
tools.description: Opens the Stateflow block library containing the Chart, State Transition Table, Truth Table and Sequence Viewer blocks.
tools.example:
sflib;
add_block('sflib/Chart', 'myModel/Supervisor');
tools.notes: The library name 'sflib' is also the prefix used with add_block.
